protocols.name: General Patient Assessment
protocols.content:
| General Patient Assessment |
| ----- |
| **● A Patient Assessment** is to be performed on **every patient** regardless of complaint or presentation. **The assessment may be modified** depending on specific presentation, **the assessment may also be temporarily paused to address immediate life threats.** |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Verify** that the scene is safe for EMS personnel.  **● Perform** scene size-up.  **○ Determine:**  ■ The nature of the call.  ■ The number of patients.  ■ The mechanism of injury **or** nature of illness.  **○ If** there are more patients than providers can sufficiently care for:  **■ Declare** Mass Casualty Incident (MCI)  **■ See** MCI Protocol  **● Control** any life-threatening bleeding.  **● Perform** primary assessment.  **○ Assess** level of consciousness.  **○ Assess** ABCDE  **■ Airway  ■ Breathing (Including Lung Sounds)  ■ Circulation  ■ Deformity/Disability  ■ Expose and Examine** as needed.  **○ Treat** immediate life threats identified during primary survey as permitted by protocols and scope of practice.  **● Perform** secondary assessment.  **○ Conduct** head-to-toe examination.  **○ Obtain** SAMPLE history.  **○ Assess** OPQRST if patient complains of pain.  **○ Obtain** vital signs.  **● Follow** other applicable protocols based on what is found during assessment. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Consider** immediate emergency transport if the patient is unstable and the issue is not immediately correctable on-scene.  **● Obtain** Blood Glucose Level (BGL) **if** the patient has altered mental status, is unconscious, or has a history of diabetes. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** cardiac monitoring by 4-lead ECG, may also consider obtaining 12-lead ECG if indicated.  **● Consider** End-Tidal CO2 (ETCO2) monitoring for patients with respiratory complaints, suspected sepsis, or other applicable issues. |

protocols.name: Pain Management
protocols.content:
| Pain Management |
| ----- |
| ● **Pain Management** should be considered in any patient who complains of pain. Pain management should be reasonable and titrated to effect. The goal of pain management is not necessarily to eliminate **all** pain, but to reduce the patient’s pain to an acceptable minimum. Less invasive and less extreme methods of pain management should always be considered before resorting to more extreme methods. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** patient in a position of comfort.  **● Splint** affected limbs in a position of comfort.  ○ Patients often self-splint prior to the arrival of EMS by holding their arms in a position of comfort. So long as this position maintains circulation in the  extremity, try to splint the limb in this position. Avoid repositioning limbs if possible.  **● Apply Ice or Cold Pack** to affected area to reduce pain and swelling. **● Elevate** extremity if possible to reduce pain and swelling. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Consider** Acetaminophen 500-1000mg PO, no repeat. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Consider** Acetaminophen 500-1000mg IV/IO for mild to severe pain, no repeat. **● Consider** Morphine 2-5mg IV/IO or 5-10mg Morphine IM.  ○ If administering IV/IO, may repeat every 3-5 minutes.  ○ If administering IM, may repeat every 20 minutes.  ○ Max total dose of 30mg.  **● Consider** Fentanyl 1mcg/kg IV/IO/IM/IN.  ○ If administering IV/IO/IN, may repeat every 5 minutes.  ○ If administering IM, may repeat every 10 minutes.  ○ Max total dose of 3mcg/kg. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Ketamine 0.3mg/kg IV/IO/IN or 0.5mg/kg IM.  ○ May repeat every 5 minutes to a max total dose of 500mg. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Ketorolac 15mg IV or 30mg IM, no repeat.  ○ **DO NOT** administer to patients with significant trauma or patients who are at a significant risk for internal bleeding. Consider all contraindications.  **● Consider** Droperidol 2.5mg IV/IO/IM, no repeat. |
| **Key Points & Considerations** |
| **● Never** establish an IO solely for the purpose of pain management. IOs may only be used for pain management in the event that they have been established for another justifiable purpose. |

protocols.name: Nausea/Vomiting
protocols.content:
| Nausea/Vomiting |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** patient in a position of comfort.  **● Provide** patient with an emesis bag, if possible.  **● Consider** having the patient sniff a 70% isopropyl alcohol prep pad, if one is available. **● If** the patient is unable to protect their own airway and is actively vomiting or about to vomit, roll the patient onto their side and suction as-needed to clear the airway. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Consider** Ondansetron 4mg IV/IO/IM/PO.  **○** May repeat every 5 minutes to a max total dose of 12mg.  **● Consider** Diphenhydramine 25mg IV/IO/IM/PO.  ○ May repeat once in five minutes to a max total dose of 50mg. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Droperidol 0.625mg IV/IO/IM, no repeat. |
| **Key Points & Considerations** |
| **● Never** establish an IO solely for the purpose of managing nausea or vomiting. IOs may only be used for the management of nausea or vomiting in the event that they have been established for another justifiable purpose. |

protocols.name: Determination of Death
protocols.content:
| Determination of Death |
| ----- |
| **● If** any of the following criteria are met, EMS personnel shall withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Valid Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) Order  ○ Must** be signed by the patient or their authorized power of attorney **and** a licensed physician.  **○ Must** also be physically present in paper form. Images or tattoos are **not** an acceptable alternative.  **● Rigor Mortis**  ○ Stiffening of the joints and muscles that takes place typically about two hours after death.  **● Lividity**  ○ A large bruise that forms as a result of the pooling of blood with gravity that results from a lack of circulation.  **● Decapacitation  ● Incineration  ● Destruction or loss of major organs.  ● Triaged as deceased or expectant at the scene of a declared MCI according to MCI protocol.**  ○ EMS personnel may initiate resuscitation on these patients in the event that on-scene EMS personnel feel that an abundance of resources exist that would allow for a resuscitation attempt to be made without withholding necessary resources from other patients. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● EMTs may discontinue ongoing efforts on a medical cardiac arrest if:** ○ No ROSC is obtained after 20 minutes of resuscitation efforts, the patient did not have a shockable rhythm at any point in time, **and** all suspected reversible causes have been treated according to their scope of practice.  **● EMTs may discontinue ongoing efforts on a traumatic cardiac arrest if:** ○ No ROSC is obtained after 10 minutes of resuscitation efforts, the patient did not have a shockable rhythm at any point in time, **and** all suspected reversible causes have been treated according to their scope of practice. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Paramedics may discontinue ongoing efforts or withhold efforts on a traumatic cardiac arrest if:**  ○ Patient is in asystole or PEA \<20. |
| **Key Points & Considerations** |
| **● Contact** EMS Physician or Base Hospital for orders to withhold or discontinue efforts on any patients outside of the criteria listed on this protocol. |

protocols.name: Airway Management
protocols.content:
| Airway Management |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Reposition** the patient's airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **● Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  ○ Either an Oropharyngeal Airway (OPA) or Nasopharyngeal Airway (NPA) for EMRs.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy or ventilatory support using a BVM as-needed. ● **Suction** as-needed. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Consider** placing an I-Gel Supraglottic Airway if the patient requires airway management and no gag reflex is present. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** endotracheal intubation if the patient requires airway management and no gag reflex is present.  **● If** the patient’s airway is obstructed and you are unable to remove the obstruction in a timely manner or ventilate the patient by any other means:  ○ **Perform** needle cricothyrotomy. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** facilitating endotracheal intubation if the patient requires airway management using induction agents, paralytics, and sedatives as-needed. ● **If** the patient’s airway is obstructed and you are unable to remove the obstruction in a timely manner or ventilate the patient by any other means:  ○ **Perform** surgical cricothyrotomy. |

protocols.name: Wheezing/Bronchospasm
protocols.content:
| Wheezing/Bronchospasm |
| ----- |
| ● **Bronchospasm** is characterized by a narrowing of the bronchi in the lungs that restricts airflow and subsequently inhibits ventilation and oxygenation. Typical assessment findings include wheezing when auscultating lung sounds with a stethoscope. Medical history may include asthma or COPD. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ Ideally, the patient should be sat upright to keep the airway in-line and make breathing as easy as possible. Some people may attempt to place their hands on their knees and assume a “tripod” position.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy in order to relieve distress and titrate SpO2 to ≥94%. **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Consider** CPAP if the patient meets criteria outlined in CPAP procedure protocol and they are in severe respiratory distress, not alleviated by less aggressive interventions. **● Administer** Albuterol 2.5mg via Nebulizer, repeat as needed.  **● Administer** Atrovent 0.5mg via Nebulizer with first dose of Albuterol, do not repeat. **● Consider** contacting Base Hospital or EMS Physician for orders to administer 0.3mg IM Epinephrine via Auto-Injector if patient condition does not improve or is rapidly getting worse. **(EMT Only)  ● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Administer** Epinephrine 0.3-0.5mg 1:1,000 IM **if** patient condition is not improving with other interventions or is rapidly getting worse.  ○ May repeat in 0.3mg doses up to 0.9mg total if necessary.  **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Administer** Magnesium Sulfate 2g IV/IO Drip **if** patient condition is not improving with less aggressive treatment interventions.  **○** Paramedics should consider administering this medication even if Epinephrine 1:1,000 has not been administered.  ○ No repeat dose.  **● Monitor** End-Tidal CO2. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Administer** Dexamethasone 10mg IV/IO/IM. |

protocols.name: Pulmonary Edema
protocols.content:
| Pulmonary Edema |
| ----- |
| ● **Pulmonary Edema** is characterized by a build-up of fluid in the lungs, typical assessment findings include the sound of crackles/rales when assessing lung sounds with a stethoscope, often associated with respiratory distress. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ Ideally, patient should be sat upright to push fluid to the bases of the lung(s) and prevent broad distribution.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy in order to relieve distress and titrate SpO2 to ≥94%. **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Consider** CPAP if no contraindications exist.  **● If** CPAP is contraindicated, provide positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● If patient has normal BP or is hypertensive, administer Nitroglycerin according to the following criteria:**  ○ SBP 100-120: 0.4mg SL  ○ SBP 120-200: 0.8mg SL  ○ SBP \>200: 1.2mg SL  ○ Withhold Nitroglycerin if SBP \<100 or patient has taken PDE-5 inhibitors in the last 24 hours.  **● If patient is hypotensive with SBP \<90:**  ○ Initiate Norepinephrine drip via IV/IO.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG.  **● Monitor** End-Tidal CO2. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Nitroglycerin IV/IO infusion as an alternative to sublingual administration. ● **Consider** Furosemide 40mg IV/IO/IM. |

protocols.name: Foreign Body Airway Obstruction (Choking/FBAO)
protocols.content:
| Foreign Body Airway Obstruction (Choking/FBAO) |
| ----- |
| ● **A Foreign Body Airway Obstruction** refers to a partial or complete blockage of the airway by a foreign body, such as food. Patients may present in a variety of manners. Conscious patients with a partial obstruction may cough violently in an attempt to dislodge the item. Conscious patients with a complete obstruction will be silent and typically bring both hands up to their neck (the universal sign of choking). Unconscious patients with a FBAO should be treated according to cardiac arrest guidelines with a strong emphasis on removing the blockage. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● If partial obstruction is suspected and patient is awake and coughing:** ○ **Encourage** the patient to continue coughing until condition changes or item is dislodged.  **● If complete obstruction is suspected, patient is awake and silent:** ○ **Position** yourself behind the patient and perform a continuous series of five abdominal thrusts followed by five back blows until condition changes or item is dislodged.  **● If patient goes unresponsive as a result of choking or is found unresponsive initially:**  ○ **Begin CPR** according to the Medical Cardiac Arrest protocol with a strong emphasis on high-quality chest compressions. Check the airway every 2 minutes during pulse checks/rhythm analysis to see if the item has been further dislodged and can now be safely removed. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● If patient is unresponsive as a result of choking and above resuscitative efforts are ongoing:**  ○ Visualize the airway with a laryngoscope and attempt to remove the object with Magill Forceps.  **● If the patient is unresponsive and the object cannot be removed with Magill Forceps:**  ○ Attempt Endotracheal Intubation  ■ If intubation is unsuccessful:  ● Perform needle cricothyrotomy. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● If patient is unresponsive and the object cannot be removed with Magill Forceps, and intubation attempt is unsuccessful:**  ○ Perform surgical cricothyrotomy. |

protocols.name: LUNG SOUNDS REFERENCE GUIDE
protocols.content:
Lung sounds should be assessed in all patients, but special attention should be paid to them in patients with respiratory complaints or known/suspected chest trauma.
((These are being provided for informational purposes only. In reality, while some patients will freely offer up a description of what would be heard when assessing their lung sounds, most will just tell you what the underlying cause of the issue is. Do not overcomplicate things, whenever you're in doubt, just ask the patient what they are trying to roleplay. Based on that, choose the most appropriate protocol to treat the patient's condition.))
**Clear**
**Description:** The audible movement of air through the lungs without any hindrance or abnormalities as heard via a stethoscope.
**Clinical Significance:** Air is moving normally through the lungs, however, this finding does not preclude the possibility of gas exchange being inhibited at a deeper level if other signs and symptoms are present. Such would be the case with a pulmonary embolism (blood clot in the lungs).
**Wheezing**
**Description:** Audible wheezing can be heard on inhalation, exhalation, or both when lung sounds are assessed using a stethoscope.
**Clinical Significance:** An obstruction is present in the lower airway, typically associated with a narrowing of the bronchi. This is an expected finding in patients complaining of shortness of breath secondary to asthma, COPD, bronchitis, smoke inhalation, or anaphylaxis.
**Rales/Crackles**
**Description:** A crackling sound can be heard when assessing lung sounds using a stethoscope.
**Clinical Significance:** Fluid is present in the lungs, otherwise known as pulmonary edema. Typically associated with congestive heart failure or drowning.
**Stridor**
**Description:** High-pitched wheezing sound originating from the upper airway, often can be heard without the use of a stethoscope.
**Clinical Significance:** An obstruction is present in the upper airway. May be due to an intrinsic factor, such as swelling, or an extrinsic factor, such as a foreign body obstruction. Typically associated with anaphylactic reactions, inhalation burns, or foreign body obstructions (choking).
**Rhonchi**
**Description:** Low-pitched and coarse sound, typically only can be heard using a stethoscope.
**Clinical Significance:** An obstruction is present in the lower airway, almost always excess mucus in the case of rhonchi. Typically associated with respiratory infections, pneumonia.
**Diminished**
**Description:** Clear, but diminished, movement of air through the lungs. **Clinical Significance:** May be due to a multitude of factors, other signs and symptoms should be accounted for when determining the clinical significance of this finding. In trauma, this finding is associated with a developing pneumothorax, hemothorax, or hemopneumothorax. In medical patients, it is often associated with severe bronchoconstriction preventing air from reaching further down into the lungs, or a physical obstruction of the alveoli, as seen in pneumonia.
**Absent**
**Description:** Lung sounds cannot be heard.
**Clinical Significance:** All associated signs and symptoms must be accounted for when making a determination. Absent lung sounds occur when there is no significant air movement through a lung. In trauma patients, this is typically associated with a pneumothorax, hemothorax, or hemopneumothorax. In medical patients, this finding may still be present due to other factors, or as the result of a spontaneous pneumothorax.

protocols.name: Chest Pain of Suspected Cardiac Origin
protocols.content:
| Chest Pain of Suspected Cardiac Origin |
| ----- |
| ● **Chest Pain of Suspected Cardiac Origin** refers to chest pain or discomfort that is, based on presentation, thought to originate as the result of a cardiac issue, such as a myocardial infarction (heart attack) or angina pectoris. This type of chest pain typically cannot be provoked or worsened by pressing down on the patient’s chest or having them take a deep breath. It may start suddenly or gradually, at rest or during physical activity. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ If the patient is already in a position of comfort, try to maintain them in that position if possible.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Administer** Aspirin 324mg PO.  **● Assist** patient in taking their own Nitroglycerin **if**:  ○ It is already prescribed to them by their physician.  ○ Their SBP is \>100.  ○ They have not taken any PDE-5 inhibitors in the last 24 hours.  ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Ondansetron (Zofran) 4mg IV/IM/PO/IO **if** nausea is present, may repeat once to total of 8mg. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG.  ○ If STEMI is identified, provide STEMI activation notice to receiving hospital. ■ Prioritize rapid transportation to STEMI receiving hospital.  **● Administer** Nitroglycerin 0.4mg SL  ○ SBP must be \>100.  ○ They have not taken any PDE-5 inhibitors in the last 24 hours.  ○ Must be no evidence of inferior STEMI (ST Elevation in leads II, III, or aVF). ○ May repeat twice in 0.4mg increments every 5 minutes up to max total of 1.2mg.  ■ Do not repeat if chest pain resolves.  **● Consider** Fentanyl or Morphine for continued pain management as outlined in pain management protocol if Nitroglycerin is contraindicated or pain persists after max dose. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Heparin 5000 units IV/IO for **CONFIRMED STEMI** suspected to be a result of ACS.  **● Consider** Nitroglycerin IV/IO infusion for suspected ACS related chest pain as an alternative to sublingual administration. |

protocols.name: Medical Cardiac Arrest
protocols.content:
| Medical Cardiac Arrest |
| ----- |
| **● A Medical Cardiac Arrest** is defined as any cardiac arrest where traumatic injuries sustained by the patient are **not** suspected to be the underlying cause. These cases place a high degree of emphasis on high-quality chest compressions, early defibrillation, and the treatment of underlying reversible causes. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Verify** that the patient does not have obvious signs of death or a valid do not resuscitate (DNR) order.  **● Initiate** continuous chest compressions.  **● Apply** AED.  **● Insert** one of the following airway adjuncts:  ○ Oropharyngeal Airway (OPA) and/or Nasopharyngeal Airway (NPA)  **● Provide** 1 breath via BVM attached to high-flow oxygen for every 10 chest compressions.  **○ DO NOT** interrupt compressions to provide breaths, provide breaths during compressions.  **● Pause** chest compressions every 2 minutes to check for a pulse and allow AED to evaluate if rhythm is shockable.  **○ If** rhythm is shockable, resume compressions while the AED charges, once charged, pause compressions and clear the patient prior to delivering the shock.  ■ **Immediately** resume compressions once shock is delivered, **DO NOT** delay resuming compressions to check for a pulse.  **○ Minimize** length of pause to no more than 10 seconds.  ● **Call ALS  ● See Reversible Causes Protocol** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Insert** I-Gel Supraglottic Airway, replacing OPA or NPA if either is already in place. **○ After** I-Gel is inserted, ventilations should be provided every 6 seconds with compressions ongoing. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply LifePak 15/Zoll X FAST pads instead of AED**. Manually evaluate rhythms every 2 minutes and defibrillate if indicated.  **● Administer** Epinephrine 1:10,000 1mg IV/IO every 3-5 minutes.  ○ It is often easiest to administer the above during every other 2 minute cycle of CPR at 4 minute intervals. |
| **Key Points & Considerations** |
| **● See Determination of Death Protocol For Discontinuation/Obvious Death Criteria.** |

protocols.name: Reversible Causes (Medical Cardiac Arrest)
protocols.content:
| Reversible Causes (Medical Cardiac Arrest) |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Opioid Overdose:  ○ Administer** 2mg Narcan IN  ■ May repeat up to 10mg total as-needed.  **● Hypothermia:  ○ Move** the patient to a warm environment, if possible, place heat packs in armpits and groins.  **● Hypoxia:  ○ Ensure** open airway and administer high-flow oxygen via bag-valve mask. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Opioid Overdose:  ○ Administer** 2mg Narcan IV/IO/IM/IN  ■ May repeat up to 10mg total as-needed.  ● **Hypothermia:  ○ Administer** Warm Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus.  ■ Max total fluid dose of 2 liters.  **● Hypovolemia:  ○ Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus.  ■ Max total fluid dose of 2 liters.  **● Hypoglycemia:  ○ Administer** Dextrose 10% Solution IV/IO  ■ Repeat as-needed to restore BGL to normal range (\>70mg/dl).  **● Tension Pneumothorax:  ○ Perform** needle decompression on the affected side or bilaterally. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Hyperkalemia  ○ Administer** Sodium Bicarbonate 1mEq/kg IV/IO push.  **● Refractory Ventricular Tachycardia (VT) or Ventricular Fibrillation (VF): ○ Defined** as shocking the patient at least twice with no successful conversion. **■ Administer one of the following antiarrhythmics:  ● Amiodarone** 300mg IV/IO push, may repeat once in 3-5  minutes at a dose of 150mg.  **● Lidocaine** 1.5mg/kg IV/IO push, may repeat every 3-5 minutes  at 0.75mg/kg no more than twice, up to a max total of 3mg/kg.  **■ Consider** a vector change, such as posterior-anterior pad placement. **■ Consider** dual sequential defibrillation.  **● Torsades De Pointes (Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia)  ○ Administer** Magnesium Sulfate 2g IV/IO push.  **● Hypocalcemia  ○ Administer** Calcium Chloride 1g IV/IO push. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Cardiac Tamponade:  ○ Perform** pericardiocentesis.  **● Tension Pneumothorax:  ○ Perform** finger thoracostomy. |

protocols.name: Tachycardia With Palpable Pulses
protocols.content:
| Tachycardia With Palpable Pulses |
| ----- |
| ● **Tachycardia With Palpable Pulses** refers to a sustained, rapid heart rate, that may or may not be the result of a cardiac dysrhythmia where palpable pulses are present. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ If the patient is already in a position of comfort, try to maintain them in that position if possible.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** patient is unstable **and** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Consider** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus based on potential underlying causes of tachycardia, especially if dehydration and/or fever/infection are suspected, or patient has SBP \<90.  ○ Exercise caution in patients who are showing evidence of fluid overload. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG  ○ May delay acquiring 12-Lead ECG if patient condition is unstable and warrants immediate intervention.  **● If rhythm other than sinus is identified:  ○ See Tachydysrhythmia With Palpable Pulses** |

protocols.name: Tachydysrhythmia With Palpable Pulses
protocols.content:
| Tachydysrhythmia With Palpable Pulses |
| ----- |
| ● **Tachydysrhythmia With Palpable Pulses** refers to an abnormal heart rhythm with a sustained heart rate greater than 100 and a palpable pulse. Presentations and underlying causes may vary. |
| **Paramedic** |
| ● **If Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT) is identified:**  ○ **Determine** if stable or unstable based on presentation and SBP being above or below 90\.  ■ **If stable**, do the following in order until rhythm converts:  ● **Attempt** Vagal Maneuver  **● Administer** Adenosine 6mg Rapid IV Push  **● Administer** Adenosine 12mg Rapid IV Push  **● Consider** Diltiazem 0.25mg/kg Slow IV Push **if** above is  unsuccessful.  **■ If unstable:**  ● **Attempt** Synchronized Cardioversion  ○ **May** repeat to a max of 3 attempts.  ○ **Consider** Midazolam 2mg IV/IO or 4mg IN prior to  cardioversion.  ● **If Rapid Atrial Fibrillation (HR \>150) is identified:  ○ Determine** if stable or unstable based on presentation and SBP being above or below 90\.  ■ **If stable**:  **● Administer** Diltiazem 0.25mg/kg Slow IV Push  ■ **If unstable:  ● Attempt** Synchronized Cardioversion.  ○ **May** repeat to a max of 3 attempts.  ○ **Consider** Midazolam 2mg IV/IO or 4mg IN prior to  cardioversion.  ● **If Monomorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (V-Tach/VT) is identified: ○ Determine** if stable or unstable based on presentation and SBP being above or below 90\.  ■ **If stable**:  ● **Administer** Amiodarone 150mg IV Drip  ■ **If unstable:  ● Attempt** Synchronized Cardioversion  ○ **May** repeat to a max of 3 attempts.  ○ **Consider** Midazolam 2mg IV/IO or 4mg IN prior to  cardioversion.  ● **If Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (Torsades) is identified:  ○ Determine** if stable or unstable based on presentation and SBP being above or below 90\.  ■ **If stable**:  ● **Administer** Magnesium Sulfate 2g IV Drip  ■ **If unstable**:  ● **Attempt** Defibrillation  ○ **May** repeat to a max of 3 attempts.  ○ **Consider** Midazolam 2mg IV/IO or 4mg IN prior to  cardioversion. |

protocols.name: Bradycardia
protocols.content:
| Bradycardia |
| ----- |
| ● **Bradycardia** refers to a low heart rate, less than 60\. For the purposes of this protocol, we only consider **symptomatic bradycardia** below a rate of 50\. That is, bradycardia that is actually causing adverse effects for the patient. Such as, hypotension, altered mental status, etc. Do not treat bradycardia simply based on the number being low if it is not causing symptoms for the patient. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ If the patient is already in a position of comfort, try to maintain them in that position if possible.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus **if** patient is symptomatic or hypotensive. ○ Exercise caution in patients who are showing evidence of fluid overload. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG  ○ May delay acquiring 12-Lead ECG if patient condition is unstable and warrants immediate intervention.  ● **Administer** Atropine 1mg IV/IO **if** patient is symptomatic and hypotensive. ○ May repeat every 3-5 minutes up to 3mg max total.  ○ Withhold for Second Degree Type II or Third Degree (Complete) Heart Blocks. ○ May consider skipping directly to Transcutaneous Pacing if patient is too unstable to delay treatment for IV/IO access to be established.  **● Initiate** Transcutaneous Pacing **if** patient is symptomatic, hypotensive, **and** Atropine is contraindicated or ineffective.  ○ **Administer** Midazolam 2mg IV/IO or 4mg IN prior to or during pacing ■ Do not delay pacing to establish IV/IO access for pain management or sedation, administer Midazolam with pacing in progress if patient  condition warrants it. **DO NOT** establish an IO solely for pain  management or sedation.  **● Administer** Epinephrine 1:100,000 10-20mcg IV/IO push **if** patient is symptomatic, hypotensive, **and** Transcutaneous Pacing is unsuccessful.  ○ May repeat as needed, no max dose.  **● Consider** Epinephrine drip **if** patient requires continuous administration of vasopressors to maintain blood pressure. |

protocols.name: CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIA REFERENCE GUIDE
protocols.content:
**((These are provided for informational purposes only, players rarely specify which rhythm they are suffering from. Use the information below to choose one and treat it according to the flow chart. Do not overthink it.))**
**Cardiac Arrest**
**Asystole (Non-Shockable)**
**{image1}**
**Pulseless Electrical Activity (PEA) (Non-Shockable)**
PEA is any rhythm other than the ones displayed in this section (asystole, v-tach of either variety, v-fib) that is present on the monitor despite the patient lacking a palpable pulse. PEA is not shockable.
**Ventricular Fibrillation (V-Fib/VF) (Shockable)**
**{image2}**
**Pulseless Monomorphic Wide Complex Tachycardia (V-Tach/VT) (Shockable) {image3}**
**Pulseless Polymorphic Wide Complex Tachycardia (Torsades) (Shockable) {image4}**
**Tachycardias**
**Sinus Tachycardia**
**{image5}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "fast".))
● ((Not a dangerous rhythm in of itself, but sometimes a factor involved with another underlying ailment.))
● Consider potential underlying causes, such as physical exertion, anxiety, pain, fever/infection, dehydration, drug use, etc.
**Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT)**
**{image6}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "very fast/dangerously fast".))
● ((Much more much common than VT or Torsades, especially in younger patients.)) ● ((Most commonly roleplayed arrhythmia on GTAW.))
● May be the result of underlying cardiac disease, dehydration, fever/infection, drug use, or electrolyte imbalances.
**Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (A-Fib RVR) {image7}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "fast or dangerously fast and irregular", with irregularity being the key distinguishing factor from SVT, VT, or Torsades.)) ● ((More common in older patients with a history of atrial fibrillation (A-Fib).)) ● ((Rarely roleplayed on GTAW.))
● May be the result of underlying cardiac disease, dehydration, fever/infection, drug use, or electrolyte imbalances.
**Rapid Atrial Flutter**
**{image8}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "fast or dangerously fast".))
● ((More common in older patients.))
● ((Rarely roleplayed on GTAW.))
● Typically the result of an underlying cardiac issue.
**Pulsing Monomorphic Wide Complex Tachycardia (V-Tach/VT) {image9}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "very fast/dangerously fast".))
● ((Less common in younger patients than SVT, and typically more serious.)) ● ((Rarely roleplayed on GTAW outside of cardiac arrest.))
● May be the result of underlying cardiac disease, drug use, or electrolyte imbalances. ● May present as pulsing or pulseless.
**Pulsing Polymorphic Wide Complex Tachycardia (Torsades)**
**{image10}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "very fast/dangerously fast".))
● ((Much rarer than normal (monomorphic) VT.))
● ((Almost never roleplayed on GTAW.))
● May be the result of underlying cardiac disease, drug use, or electrolyte imbalances. But is often associated with congenital heart problems like Long QT Syndrome. ● May present as pulsing or pulseless.
**Bradycardias**
**Sinus Bradycardia**
**{image11}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "slow".))
● ((Considered to be a normal finding in athletes.))
● ((May be associated with severe head injuries and increased intracranial pressure when seen in trauma patients.))
● Only treat if symptomatic of low cardiac output.
**First Degree Heart Block**
**{image12}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "slow".))
● ((Result of a mild block in the heart's electrical conduction pathway that slows down transmissions. Usually not the cause of emergent cardiac issues.))
● ((More common in older patients.))
● ((Almost never roleplayed on GTAW.))
● Only treat if symptomatic of low cardiac output.
**Second Degree Type I Heart Block (Mobitz I/Wenckebach)**
**{image13}**● ((Typically described in roleplay as "slow or dangerously slow".))
● ((Result of a moderate block in the heart's electrical conduction pathway that slows down and occasionally blocks transmissions.))
● ((More common in older patients.))
● ((Almost never roleplayed on GTAW.))
● Only treat if symptomatic of low cardiac output.
**Second Degree Heart Type II Block (Mobitz II)**
● ((Typically described in roleplay as "slow or dangerously slow".))
● ((Result of a serious block in the heart's electrical conduction pathway that routinely blocks transmissions.))
● ((More common in older patients.))
● ((Almost never roleplayed on GTAW.))
● Atropine is ineffective in treating this rhythm.
● Only treat if symptomatic of low cardiac output.
**Third Degree Block (Complete Heart Block)**
● ((Typically described in roleplay as "dangerously slow".))
● ((Result of a serious block in the heart's electrical conduction pathway that blocks all transmissions between the top and bottom of the heart.))
● ((More common in older patients.))
● ((Almost never roleplayed on GTAW.))
● Atropine is ineffective in treating this rhythm.
● Only treat if symptomatic of low cardiac output.

protocols.name: Opioid/Opiate Overdose
protocols.content:
| Opioid/Opiate Overdose |
| ----- |
| ● **Opioid/Opiate Overdose** refers to an overdose of opioids or opiates that has resulted in respiratory depression. Patients who meet overdose criteria will typically present as having an altered level of consciousness, slow and shallow respirations, and pinpoint pupils. Patients who have taken opiates or opioids who are **not altered** and **do not have slow or shallow respirations** do **not** meet overdose criteria. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. ● **Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  ○ Preferably an NPA if no facial trauma is present to avoid triggering gag reflex after Narcan administration.  ● **Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen. **● Suction** as-needed.  **● Administer** Narcan 2mg IN, may repeat up to max dose of 10mg.  ○ Only administer enough Narcan to restore respiratory drive and allow the patient to breathe on their own sufficiently.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available and patient condition is not improving with the above treatment. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Consider** Narcan 0.4-2mg IV/IO/IM |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor. |

protocols.name: Beta Blocker/Calcium Channel Blocker Overdose
protocols.content:
| Beta Blocker/Calcium Channel Blocker Overdose |
| ----- |
| ● **Beta Blocker/Calcium Channel Blocker Overdose** refers to a patient who has overdosed on beta blockers or calcium channel blockers and is symptomatic as a result. Patients will typically present as severely bradycardic, hypotensive, altered, and lethargic or unconscious. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus  ○ Exercise caution in patients who are showing evidence of fluid overload. **● If** patient is responsive, able to swallow, and oral ingestion is suspected within the last hour:  **○ Administer** Activated Charcoal 1g/kg PO |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG  ○ May delay acquiring 12-Lead ECG if patient condition is unstable and warrants immediate intervention.  **● Administer** Atropine 1mg IV/IO for associated symptomatic bradycardia. ○ May repeat every 3-5 minutes up to 3mg max total.  **● Administer** Epinephrine 1:100,000 10-20mcg IV/IO push **if** Atropine does not sufficiently improve patient condition.  ○ May repeat as needed, no max dose.  ● **Initiate** Transcutaneous Pacing **if** neither Atropine or Epinephrine are effective in sufficiently improving patient condition. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Insert** Nasogastric (NG) Tube or Orogastric (OG) Tube **if** patient is altered and unable to swallow or intubated **and** oral ingestion is suspected within the last hour. ○ **Suction** gastric contents.  ○ **Administer** Activated Charcoal 1g/kg via NG/OG Tube. |

protocols.name: Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose
protocols.content:
| Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose |
| ----- |
| ● **Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose** refers to a patient who has overdosed on tricyclic antidepressants. Patients may initially present as symptomatic or asymptomatic. Symptomatic patients may present with mild, moderate, or severe symptoms depending on amount ingested. Symptoms may range from tachycardia, dry mouth, nausea and vomiting, and agitation to altered mental status,  unresponsiveness, and cardiac dysrhythmias. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ Consider placing the patient on the left side in the recovery position if they are lethargic and/or nauseated.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus  ○ Exercise caution in patients who are showing evidence of fluid overload. **● If** patient is responsive, able to swallow, and oral ingestion is suspected within the last hour:  **○ Administer** Activated Charcoal 1g/kg PO |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG  ○ May delay acquiring 12-Lead ECG if patient condition is unstable and warrants immediate intervention.  ● **Administer** Sodium Bicarbonate 1mEq/kg IV/IO, may repeat dose once if necessary. **● If** seizure is present or occurs:  **○ Administer** Midazolam (Versed) 2-5mg IV/IO **OR** 10mg IM  ■ May repeat once if seizure continues longer than 5 minutes. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Insert** Nasogastric (NG) Tube or Orogastric (OG) Tube **if** patient is altered and unable to swallow or intubated **and** oral ingestion is suspected within the last hour. ○ **Suction** gastric contents.  ○ **Administer** Activated Charcoal 1g/kg via NG/OG Tube. |

protocols.name: Organophosphate Exposure
protocols.content:
| Organophosphate Exposure |
| ----- |
| **● Organophosphate Exposure** is characterized by a patient being exposed to a potentially lethal dose of organophosphates. Organophosphate exposure can occur as the result of a workplace accident or intentional attack. Organophosphates can be absorbed through the skin, via ingestion, or via inhalation. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Contact HazMat Specialists  ● Exercise extreme caution** prior to making patient contact, **DO NOT** approach the patient without appropriate PPE if any route other than oral ingestion is suspected, or if organophosphates are still potentially present and pose a danger to first responders. ● **Decontaminate the patient.  ○ Remove** contaminated clothing.  **○ If** agent is dry, brush it off.  **○ If** agent is wet, flush with copious amounts of water.  **○ If** eyes are affected, flush with normal saline.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● If** made available by LS County EMSA or LSFD EMS Bureau Command **○ Administer** CHEMPACK Autoinjector **if** patient is severely symptomatic from exposure, especially if they are experiencing bradycardia or hypotension as a result of the exposure.  ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  ● **Consider** Ondansetron (Zofran) 4mg IV/IO/PO/IM for nausea/vomiting, if present. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Administer** Atropine 2-4mg IV/IO **if** patient is severely symptomatic from exposure, especially if they are experiencing bradycardia or hypotension as a result of the exposure.  **● Administer** Midazolam (Versed) 2-5mg IV/IO **OR** 10mg IM **if** patient is seizing. ○ May repeat once if seizure continues longer than 5 minutes. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Insert** Nasogastric (NG) Tube or Orogastric (OG) Tube **if** patient is altered and unable to swallow or intubated **and** oral ingestion is suspected within the last hour. ○ **Suction** gastric contents.  ○ **Administer** Activated Charcoal 1g/kg via NG/OG Tube. |

protocols.name: Smoke Inhalation
protocols.content:
| Smoke Inhalation |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ Consider placing the patient on the left side in the recovery position if they are lethargic and/or nauseated.  ● **Provide** 15LPM Oxygen via non-rebreather if CO poisoning is suspected or the patient has any amount of respiratory distress or shortness of breath.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| ● **Consider** nebulized saline.  **● If** wheezes are present upon auscultation of lung sounds, treat according to wheezing/bronchospasm protocol.  **● Consider** CPAP if pulmonary edema is suspected. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● If** patient is seizing:  **○ Administer** Midazolam 10mg IM/IN **OR** 2-5mg IV/IO  ■ May repeat if necessary up to max total of 20mg. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** endotracheal intubation if the patient requires airway management and no gag reflex is present.  **● If** the patient’s airway is obstructed and you are unable to intubate or ventilate the patient by any other means:  ○ **Perform** needle cricothyrotomy. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● If** patient is showing signs of neurological incapacitation, such as ALOC, unconsciousness, or convulsions:  **○ Administer** Hydroxocobalamin (CyanoKit) 5g IV/IO over 15 minutes  **● If** the patient’s airway is obstructed and you are unable to intubate or ventilate the patient by any other means:  ○ **Perform** surgical cricothyrotomy. |

protocols.name: Allergic Reaction/Anaphylaxis
protocols.content:
| Allergic Reaction/Anaphylaxis |
| ----- |
| **● Allergic Reactions** are an overreaction by the immune system in response to a substance that would otherwise typically be harmless, or even beneficial, to most people. Patients may present anywhere within the range of a mild reaction, often characterized by a local rash or hives, to a severe systemic reaction that causes the patient’s airway to close and blood pressure to drop. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ○ Ideally, the patient should be sat upright to keep the airway in-line and make breathing as easy as possible. Some people may attempt to place their hands on their knees and assume a “tripod” position.  **● Provide** oxygen therapy in order to relieve distress and titrate SpO2 to ≥94%. **● If** the reaction affects the patient’s ability to breathe, the patency of their airway, **or** two 1:1,000or more distinct body systems:  **○ Assist** the patient in using their own Epi-Pen IM **if** one has been prescribed to them by their physician.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● If** patient meets above-listed criteria for Epi-Pen administration:  **○ Administer** Epi-Pen IM  ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** 0.3-0.5mg Epinephrine 1:1,000 IM **if** patient meets above mentioned criteria.  ○ May repeat up to three times if needed, max total dose of 0.9mg.  **● Administer** 50mg Benadryl IV/IM  **● If** wheezing is present upon assessment of lung sounds:  **○ Administer** Albuterol 2.5mg via Nebulizer, repeat as needed.  **○ Administer** Atrovent 0.5mg via Nebulizer with first dose of Albuterol, do not repeat.  ● **Consider** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Administer** Dexamethasone 10mg IV/IO/IM. |

protocols.name: Altered Mental Status (AMS/ALOC)
protocols.content:
| Altered Mental Status (AMS/ALOC) |
| ----- |
| **● Altered Mental Status** also commonly known as Altered Level of Consciousness (ALOC) refers to any form of decreased mental function or level of consciousness beyond what is normal for the patient. Patients may present in any range between being mildly confused to being completely unconscious. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** patient in a position of comfort.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Obtain** Blood Glucose Level (BGL)  **○ If** Blood Glucose Level is low (\<70mg/dl) **and** patient is able to swallow: **■ Administer** Oral Glucose Gel  **● Recheck** BGL after administration, repeat dose if necessary.  **○ If** Blood Glucose Level is normal (\>70mg/gl)  **■ Consider** other possible causes such as:  **● Alcohol Intoxication  ● Infection/Sepsis  ● Overdose  ● Trauma  ● Seizure  ● Cardiac Issue  ● Stroke  ■ See** other applicable protocols if cause other than hypoglycemia is  suspected.  ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| ● **Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Dextrose 10% Solution IV/IO **if** hypoglycemia (BGL \<70mg/dl) is present **and** patient is unable to swallow Oral Glucose Gel.  **○ Consider** Glucagon 1mg IM **if** IV access cannot be obtained and IO is deemed avoidable. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG |

protocols.name: Behavioral Emergencies
protocols.content:
| Behavioral Emergencies |
| ----- |
| **● Behavioral Emergencies** are defined as any instance where the behavior of an individual makes them an imminent threat to themselves or others. Patients may present with this type of behavior as a result of a wide variety of potential underlying conditions, some of which are psychiatric in nature, others may be the result of acute drug or alcohol intoxication, an underlying medical condition, or injury. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Attempt** verbal de-escalation.  ○ **Use** non-judgemental language and speak calmly to the patient.  **● Consider** potential underlying medical causes, such as:  ○ Hypoglycemia  ○ Hypoxia (SpO2 \<94%)  ○ Overdose/Intoxication  ○ Postictal State (Post-Seizure)  ○ Head Injury  **○ See** other applicable protocols if any of the above are suspected as a potential underlying cause for the patient’s behavior.  **● If** the patient is physically combative, place the patient in physical restraints. **○ EMS** personnel are **only** permitted to use prior-approved 4-point soft physical restraints attached to the gurney.  **○ Law Enforcement** personnel may opt to place the patient in handcuffs **according to policies set by their respective agency.  ○ Ensure** that restraints **DO NOT** compromise the patient’s ability to breathe, their circulation, or neurological function.  **○ Monitor** restrained patients closely and continuously reassess the patient, their respirations, circulation, and neurological function. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Monitor** patient closely during transport, do not agitate the patient.  **● If** the patient is handcuffed, law enforcement personnel **must** maintain a continuous presence. Either in the ambulance or by following directly behind. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Consider** contacting Base Hospital or EMS Physician for orders to administer 2-5mg Midazolam IV/IO/IM/IN push **if** patient remains a danger to self or others despite existing efforts to physically restrain the patient.  ● **Consider** Olanzapine 10mg ODT. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** chemical restraints **if** patient remains a danger to self or others despite existing efforts to physically restrain the patient. Approved chemical restraints include: ○ Midazolam 2-5mg IV/IO/IM/IN  ○ Ketamine 2mg/kg IV/IO/IM/IN  ● **Apply** Cardiac Monitor. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Droperidol 5mg IV/IO/IM as an alternative to the above listed options of behavioral sedation.  ○ May repeat once at 2.5mg. |

protocols.name: Seizures
protocols.content:
| Seizures |
| ----- |
| **● Seizures** are bursts of abnormal electrical activity within the brain that can cause partial or full body convulsions and a loss of consciousness. It is important to note that not all seizures present with full body convulsions, some seizures may only present with partial or localized convulsions, or no convulsions at all. |
| **EMR+** |
| **● If** the patient is **no longer seizing**:  ○ **Place** patient in a position of comfort.  ○ **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **○ Treat** any injuries the patient sustained.  **○ If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ■ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust  maneuvers.  **■ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **■ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to  high-flow oxygen if necessary.  **● If** the patient is **actively seizing**:  **○ Allow** the patient to seize.  **○ Clear** the area around the patient if necessary to prevent injury.  ○ **Provide** high-flow oxygen therapy via non-rebreather mask.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. ○ Only transport the patient when seizure resolves or it is otherwise safe to do so if seizure is not resolving.  **● Obtain** Blood Glucose Level (BGL)  **○ If** Blood Glucose Level is low (\<70mg/dl) **and** patient is able to swallow: **■ Administer** Oral Glucose Gel  **● Recheck** BGL after administration, repeat dose if necessary. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● If** the patient is **actively seizing**:  **○ Administer** Midazolam 10mg IM/IN **OR** 2-5mg IV/IO  ■ May repeat if necessary up to max total of 20mg.  **● Administer** Dextrose 10% Solution IV/IO drip **if** hypoglycemia (BGL\<70mg/dl) is suspected cause of ALOC **and** patient is unable to swallow Oral Glucose Gel. **○ Consider** Glucagon 1mg IM **if** IV access cannot be obtained. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG  **● Consider** eclampsia, if the patient is pregnant, see Preeclampsia/Eclampsia Protocol. ● **Administer** Ketamine 1mg/kg IV/IO/IM for status seizures which are not terminated by midazolam. |

protocols.name: Sepsis
protocols.content:
| Sepsis |
| ----- |
| **● Sepsis** occurs when the body overreacts to an infection, causing widespread inflammation, vasodilation, fluid loss, and organ damage. Patients will typically present in a fashion which indicates the presence of some type of systemic infectious disease. Among the most important potential findings, patients may have a fever, elevated heart rate, elevated respiratory rate, low blood pressure, or altered level of consciousness. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Assess** patient to see if they meet SIRS criteria:  ○ Tachycardia (HR \>90)  ○ Tachypnea (RR \>20)  ○ Hypotension (Systolic BP \>90)  ○ Fever OR Hypothermia  **○ If** patient is positive for **any two** of the above with no other reasonable explanation, patient meets sepsis criteria.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Obtain** Blood Glucose Level (BGL)  **○ If** Blood Glucose Level is low **and** patient is symptomatic, see ALOC protocol. ● **Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. ● **Consider** Acetaminophen 500-1000mg PO for fever, no repeat. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus  ○ Exercise caution in patients who are showing evidence of fluid overload. **● Consider** Acetaminophen 500-1000mg IV/IO for fever, no repeat. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Epinephrine 1:100,000 10-20mcg IV/IO push **if** patient remains hypotensive despite fluid administration.  ○ May repeat as needed, no max dose.  ● **Consider** Epinephrine or norepinephrine drip **if** patient requires continuous administration of vasopressors to maintain blood pressure. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Consider** Ceftriaxone 2g IV/IO drip over 10 minutes and 80mg Gentamicin IM if patient meets SIRS criteria. |

protocols.name: Stroke/CVA
protocols.content:
| Stroke/CVA |
| ----- |
| **● Stroke/CVA** occurs when blood flow in the brain is interrupted by the presence of a clot or hemorrhage. Subsequently, the portion of the brain starved for oxygen begins to fail. Stroke patients may present with weakness on one side of the body, facial droop, sudden vision changes, nausea/vomiting, an altered level of consciousness, etc. Time is a critical resource for these patients, stroke patients need to be rapidly identified and transported to an appropriate receiving hospital. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● Perform** Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale (CPSS) Assessment  **○ Assess** for facial droop, ask the patient to smile. If facial droop is present, consider that a positive result.  **○ Assess** arm drift, ask patient to close eyes and extend arms outward with palms facing up and to hold them for 10 seconds, if one arm drifts down, patient is unable to hold that arm out for 10 seconds, consider that a positive result.  **○ Assess** speech, ask patient to say a familiar or common phrase such as “The Sky is Always Sunny in Cincinnati”. If they are unable to do so without slurring, consider that a positive result.  **○ If** any of the above turn up a positive result, and the positive deficit is new onset and not preexisting, patient meets stroke activation criteria.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. ○ Rapid transport is a priority.  **● Obtain** Blood Glucose Level (BGL)  **○ If** Blood Glucose Level is low **and** patient is symptomatic, see ALOC protocol. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  ○ Strongly prefer 18G IV access in upper forearm or AC. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| ● **If** the patient is in a symptomatic hypertensive emergency (SBP \>220) due to suspected CVA:  ○ **Administer** Labetalol 20mg, slow IV/IO push, to a target of SBP \<185 ■ **If** the patient remains hypertensive, repeat 40mg at 10 minutes. |

protocols.name: Head, Neck, and Facial Trauma
protocols.content:
| Head, Neck, and Facial Trauma |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Control** any life-threatening bleeding.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy in order to relieve distress and titrate SpO2 to ≥94%. **● Consider** if spinal motion restriction (SMR) is indicated.  **● If patient’s airway is compromised or patient is not breathing sufficiently: ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen as-needed.  **○ Suction** as-needed.  **● Stabilize** impaled objects, if present.  **○ DO NOT REMOVE UNLESS PATIENT’S AIRWAY CANNOT BE MANAGED BY ANY OTHER METHOD OR CPR CANNOT BE PERFORMED.  ○ If** object is impaled in the patient’s eye, cover both eyes to prevent movement. **● Bandage** wounds and control lesser bleeding as indicated.  **● Splint** injuries as-needed. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Prioritize** rapid transport for unstable patients, treat immediate life threats prior to initiating transport, if possible.  **● Elevate** the patient’s head 20° if possible. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus **if** systolic BP is \<90.  ○ Only administer enough fluids to maintain systolic BP around 90  ○ **If** the patient is suspected to have a serious head injury, aim for a systolic BP target of 110 to maintain adequate cerebral perfusion.  ● **Administer** Tranexamic Acid (TXA) 2g slow IV/IO push for suspected hemorrhagic shock (SBP \<90) or GCS of 12 or less secondary to head trauma.  ● **If** the patient is **actively seizing**:  **○ Administer** Midazolam 10mg IM/IN **OR** 2-5mg IV/IO  ■ May repeat if necessary up to max total of 20mg. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Administer** Epinephrine 1:100,000 10-20mcg IV/IO Push **if** neurogenic shock is suspected.  ○ May repeat every 2-5 minutes as needed, no max dose.  ● **Consider** Warmed Whole Blood IV/IO if hemorrhagic shock is suspected. **(IF AVAILABLE)  ● If** the patient’s airway is compromised and cannot be managed by any other means: ○ Perform needle cricothyrotomy. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● If** the patient has extensive soft tissue trauma, life/limb threatening penetrating trauma, or significant dog bite wounds and no known allergy to cephalosporins:  **○ Administer** Ceftriaxone 2g IV/IO/IM.  ● **Consider** 3% Hypertonic Saline 250ml IV/IO bolus over 15 minutes for GCS of 8 or less secondary to head trauma.  ● **Consider** Levetiracetam 1500mg IV/IO/IM for GCS of 8 or less secondary to head trauma.  ● **If** the patient’s airway is compromised and cannot be managed by any other means: ○ Perform surgical cricothyrotomy. |

protocols.name: Chest, Abdominal, Pelvic Trauma
protocols.content:
| Chest, Abdominal, Pelvic Trauma |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Control** any life-threatening bleeding.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy in order to relieve distress and titrate SpO2 to ≥94%. **● Consider** if spinal motion restriction (SMR) is indicated.  **● If patient’s airway is compromised or patient is not breathing sufficiently: ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen as-needed.  **○ Suction** as-needed.  **● Stabilize** impaled objects, if present.  **○ DO NOT REMOVE UNLESS PATIENT’S AIRWAY CANNOT BE MANAGED BY ANY OTHER METHOD OR CPR CANNOT BE PERFORMED.  ○ If** object is impaled in the patient’s eye, cover both eyes to prevent movement. **● If flail chest is present**, stabilize with bulky dressings.  ● **If organs are exposed**, cover with wet sterile dressings.  **○ DO NOT ATTEMPT TO PLACE ORGANS BACK INTO THE PATIENT. ● If pelvis is unstable**, apply pelvic binder.  **● If open chest wound is present with air leak**, apply occlusive dressing and tape on three sides or use a vented chest seal.  **● Bandage** wounds and control lesser bleeding as indicated.  **● Splint** injuries as-needed. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Prioritize** rapid transport for unstable patients, treat immediate life threats prior to initiating transport, if possible. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● If tension pneumothorax is suspected**, perform needle decompression. **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus **if** systolic BP is \<90.  ○ Allow permissive hypotension, only administer enough fluids to maintain systolic BP around 90-100.  ● **Administer** Tranexamic Acid (TXA) 2g slow IV/IO push **if** systolic BP is \<90 **and** hemorrhagic shock is suspected as the underlying cause. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Administer** Epinephrine 1:100,000 10-20mcg IV/IO Push **if** neurogenic shock is suspected.  ○ May repeat as needed, no max dose.  ● **Consider** Warmed Whole Blood IV/IO if hemorrhagic shock is suspected. **(IF AVAILABLE)** |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| ● **Consider** finger thoracostomy as an alternative to needle decompression. **● Consider** eFAST exam using POCUS.  **● Perform** pericardiocentesis if cardiac tamponade is diagnosed on ultrasound. **● If** the patient has extensive soft tissue trauma, life/limb threatening penetrating trauma, or significant dog bite wounds and no known allergy to cephalosporins:  **○ Administer** Ceftriaxone 2g IV/IO/IM. |

protocols.name: Extremity Trauma
protocols.content:
| Extremity Trauma |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Control** any life-threatening bleeding.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy in order to relieve distress and titrate SpO2 to ≥94%. **● Consider** if spinal motion restriction (SMR) is indicated.  **● If patient’s airway is compromised or patient is not breathing sufficiently: ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen as-needed.  **○ Suction** as-needed.  **● Stabilize** impaled objects, if present.  **● Bandage** wounds and control lesser bleeding as indicated.  **● Splint** injuries as-needed. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Prioritize** rapid transport for unstable patients, treat immediate life threats prior to initiating transport, if possible.  **● Apply** traction splint **if** closed mid-shaft femur fracture is suspected. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus **if** systolic BP is \<90.  ○ Allow permissive hypotension, only administer enough fluids to maintain systolic BP around 90-100.  ● **Administer** Tranexamic Acid (TXA) 2g slow IV/IO push **if** bleeding is severe and cannot be controlled by tourniquets, direct pressure, packing, etc. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● If** limb is deformed **and** lacks distal circulation, make **one attempt** to manipulate the limb or reduce the fracture in order to restore circulation.  ○ Splint in place if circulation is successfully restored.  ○ If circulation cannot be restored after one attempt, splint in a position of comfort (if possible) and transport.  ● **Consider** Warmed Whole Blood IV/IO if hemorrhagic shock is suspected. **(IF AVAILABLE)** |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● If** the patient has an open longbone fracture, extensive soft tissue trauma, life/limb threatening penetrating trauma, or significant dog bite wounds and no known allergy to cephalosporins:  **○ Administer** Ceftriaxone 2g IV/IO/IM. |

protocols.name: Spinal Motion Restriction (SMR)
protocols.content:
| Spinal Motion Restriction (SMR) |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Determine** if SMR is indicated.  ○ **Consider** the Mechanism of Injury (MOI)  ■ Significant MVA?  ■ Significant fall from height or onto a hard surface?  ■ Potential direct trauma to the spine?  ■ Etc.  **○ Examine** the patient for any of the following:  ■ Midline neck or upper back pain.  ■ Distal numbness, tingling, or paralysis.  ■ Palpable spinal deformity.  **○ Consider** factors that may affect your ability to perform an accurate  assessment:  ■ Patient has altered mental status (AMS) or is unconscious.  ■ Patient is suspected to have used substances that may impair their  ability to perceive pain.  ■ Patient has distracting injuries that may draw their focus away from  their spine and impair their ability to accurately “pin-point” pain.  **○ If** the patient meets any of the criteria listed under the “examine” portion listed above **or** has experienced a significant MOI **and** an accurate assessment is not possible:  **■ Apply** spinal motion restriction.  ● Spinal motion restriction may be achieved through the use of  manual stabilization, a rigid cervical collar, a soft cervical collar,  or by padding around the patient’s neck with towels, blankets, or  pillows.  **○ Avoid** the use of rigid cervical collars on patients who  are suspected to be suffering from moderate to severe  head injuries (GCS 12 or less secondary to head  trauma) or patients who may suffer airway compromise  as a result of SMR.  **● If the patient is alert and capable of walking in a safe  manner**, allow the patient to do so with appropriate SMR  applied.  **● If the patient is incapable of walking in a safe manner**, a  combi-board or scoop stretcher may be used **temporarily** to  move the patient to the gurney.  **○ Once the patient is on the gurney, remove the  combi-board or scoop stretcher from beneath them.  ■ DO NOT** leave the patient restrained to a  backboard or similar device once they are on the  gurney. |
| **Key Points & Considerations** |
| **●** The use of traditional backboards, even for extrication, should be avoided if at all possible. Combi-boards or scoop stretchers are preferred.  ● **DO NOT leave patients restrained to a backboard, combi-board, scoop stretcher, or similar device.** These devices are intended to be used **ONLY** to facilitate extrication if providers believe they are the best option available to minimize spinal motion while the patient is being moved to the gurney.  ● There is no role for SMR in patients suspected to be suffering from a spinal injury secondary to penetrating trauma. |

protocols.name: Burns
protocols.content:
| Burns |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Stop** the burning process.  **○ Chemical Burns:  ■ If it is a dry chemical**, brush as much of it off as possible prior to  flushing the area with copious amounts of sterile water.  **■ If it is not a dry chemical**, flush the area with copious amounts of  sterile water.  **○ Thermal Burns:  ■ Cool** the area with copious amounts of sterile water for no more than 5 minutes.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen.  ○ **Suction** as-needed.  **● Determine** the severity of the burns **and** the % of total body surface affected. **● Dress** burns with sterile dressings and keep the patient warm. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Administer** humidified oxygen by nebulizing normal saline **if** inhalation burns are suspected. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  ● **Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus **if** the patient has partial or full-thickness burns covering \>9% of their TBSA. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** cardiac monitor.  **● Perform** endotracheal intubation **if** inhalation burns with progressive swelling of the airway is suspected.  **○ If** intubation is unsuccessful due to airway swelling:  ■ **Perform** needle cricothyrotomy.  ● Paramedics with training on surgical cricothyrotomy, may  perform that procedure instead, as outlined below.  ● **Obtain** 12-Lead ECG **if** electrical burn is suspected. |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| ● **If** the patient’s airway is compromised and cannot be managed by any other means: ○ Perform surgical cricothyrotomy.  ● **If** burns restrict chest wall expansion and prevent effective breathing: ○ Perform chest wall escharotomy |

protocols.name: Traumatic Cardiac Arrest
protocols.content:
| Traumatic Cardiac Arrest |
| ----- |
| **● A Traumatic Cardiac Arrest** is defined as any cardiac arrest where traumatic injuries sustained by the patient are suspected to be the underlying cause. With traumatic arrests, it is crucial to prioritize treating reversible causes early in order to increase the patient’s likelihood of survival. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Verify** that the patient does not have injuries incompatible with life.  ● **Control** any life-threatening bleeding.  **○ DO NOT initiate chest compressions without first controlling significant external bleeding.  ● Initiate** chest compressions.  **● Apply** AED.  **● Insert** one of the following airway adjuncts:  ○ Oropharyngeal Airway (OPA) and/or Nasopharyngeal Airway (NPA)  **● Provide** 2 breaths via BVM attached to high-flow oxygen for every 30 chest compressions.  **● Pause** chest compressions every 2 minutes to check for a pulse and allow AED to evaluate if rhythm is shockable.  **○ If** rhythm is shockable, resume compressions while the AED charges, once charged, pause compressions and clear the patient prior to delivering the shock.  ■ **Immediately** resume compressions once shock is delivered, **DO NOT** delay resuming compressions to check for a pulse. |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Insert** I-Gel Supraglottic Airway  **○ After** I-Gel is inserted, chest compressions become continuous, only pausing every 2 minutes to check pulse and evaluate rhythm. Ventilations should be provided every 6 seconds with compressions ongoing.  ● **See Reversible Causes Protocol** |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● See Reversible Causes Protocol** |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply LifePak 15/Zoll X FAST pads instead of AED**. Manually evaluate rhythms every 2 minutes and defibrillate if indicated.  **● See Reversible Causes Protocol** |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Use** POCUS to assess for pseudo-PEA, cardiac tamponade, pneumothorax, or hemothorax. |
| **Key Points & Considerations** |
| **● See Determination of Death Protocol For Discontinuation/Obvious Death Criteria.** |

protocols.name: Reversible Causes (Traumatic Cardiac Arrest)
protocols.content:
| Reversible Causes (Traumatic Cardiac Arrest) |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Hypovolemia  ○ Control** major external bleeding, do not perform compressions if major external hemorrhage is not under control.  **○ Splint** long bone fractures, such as the femur or humerus.  **○ Apply** pelvic binder if pelvic trauma is suspected.  **○ If** partial or full thickness burns are present and covering \>9% of the patient’s total body surface area, cover with moist sterile dressings.  **● Oxygenation  ○ Ensure** open airway and administer high-flow oxygen via bag-valve mask. **● Tension Pneumothorax  ○ Call ALS  ● Tamponade (Cardiac)  ○ Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Oxygenation  ○ Insert** I-Gel Supraglottic Airway, replacing OPA or NPA if either is already in place. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Hypovolemia  ○ Administer** Warm Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus.  ■ Max total fluid dose of 2 liters.  **○ Administer** Tranexamic Acid (TXA) 2g slow IV/IO push **if** internal bleeding is suspected.  **● Tension Pneumothorax  ○ Perform** bilateral needle decompression.  **■ If** ineffective, request finger thoracostomy capable ALS provider or  initiate immediate transport with resuscitative efforts ongoing. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Oxygenation  ○ Consider** advanced airway management if indicated, such as endotracheal intubation or cricothyrotomy if the airway cannot be secured by other means. **● Hypovolemia  ○ Administer** Warmed Whole Blood IV/IO. **(IF AVAILABLE)** |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| **● Cardiac Tamponade:  ○ Perform** pericardiocentesis.  **● Tension Pneumothorax:  ○ Perform** finger thoracostomy. |

protocols.name: Childbirth
protocols.content:
| Childbirth |
| ----- |
| **EMR+** |
| **● Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● Determine** if birth is imminent.  **○ If birth is imminent:  ■ Determine** what is presenting:  **● Head** (Normal)  **● Arm(s)  ● Bottom or Leg(s)** (Breech)  **● Prolapsed Umbilical Cord  ● If the head is presenting:  ○ Proceed** with normal delivery, support head as infant is delivered, suction mouth and nose as needed, dry and stimulate the newborn immediately after delivery and assess APGAR 1 and 5 minutes after birth. Clamp and cut the umbilical cord after delivery.  ● **If an arm is presenting:  ○ Place** the patient on her left side and arrange for immediate transport via ambulance.  ● **If the bottom or legs are presenting:  ○ Attempt** to support the head and deliver the infant.  **■ If** you are unable to deliver the infant, arrange for immediate transport via ambulance.  **● If** a prolapsed umbilical cord is presenting:  **○ Check** the cord for a pulse.  **■ If** no pulse is present, insert gloved hand to relieve pressure off the cord and maintain hand in that position until patient is delivered to the  hospital and physician taking over care orders you to remove your  hand.  **○ Elevate** the patient’s legs and keep her tilted onto her left side.  **○ Wrap** the cord in moist, sterile dressings.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● If** birth is imminent and safe on-scene delivery is possible, delay transport and deliver on scene.  **● If** safe on-scene delivery is not possible or birth is complicated, do not delay transport. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  ● **Consider** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor. |

protocols.name: Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)
protocols.content:
| Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) |
| ----- |
| **● Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)** is defined as excessive bleeding after giving birth. |
| **EMR+** |
| ● **Place** the patient in a position of comfort.  **● Control** bleeding by placing sterile dressings **over not inside** the affected area. ● **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **● If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ○ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust maneuvers. **○ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **○ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to high-flow oxygen as-needed.  **● Attempt** fundal massage.  ● **Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Normal Saline IV/IO Fluid Bolus **if** systolic BP is \<90.  ○ Allow permissive hypotension, only administer enough fluids to maintain systolic BP around 90-100. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● Administer** Oxytocin 10 units IM or 10 units IV/IO drip **if** PPH is present **after the conclusion of all births and the delivery of the placenta.  ○ If** Oxytocin is ineffective and significant bleeding continues:  **■ Administer** 1g Tranexamic Acid slow IV/IO push.  ● **Administer** Warmed Whole Blood IV/IO **if** hemorrhagic shock is suspected. **(IF AVAILABLE)** |

protocols.name: Preeclampsia/Eclampsia
protocols.content:
| Preeclampsia/Eclampsia |
| ----- |
| ● **Preeclampsia** is a condition that affects pregnant women who are typically more than 20 weeks into their pregnancy, it is characterized by hypertension and the presence of protein in the patient’s urine. **Preeclampsia becomes eclampsia when the patient experiences seizures at any point during pregnancy or up to 6 weeks post-pregnancy.** |
| **EMR+** |
| **● If** the patient is **no longer seizing**:  ○ **Place** patient in a position of comfort.  ○ **Provide** oxygen therapy **if** necessary to titrate SpO2 to ≥94%.  **○ Treat** any injuries the patient sustained.  **○ If patient is unresponsive or not maintaining their airway:  ■ Reposition** patient’s airway as needed using head-tilt or jaw-thrust  maneuvers.  **■ Place** appropriate approved airway adjunct.  **■ Provide** positive-pressure ventilations using a BVM attached to  high-flow oxygen if necessary.  **● If** the patient is **actively seizing**:  **○ Allow** the patient to seize.  **○ Clear** the area around the patient if necessary to prevent injury.  **● Call ALS** |
| **EMT+** |
| **● Do NOT** delay transport **if** ALS is substantially delayed or not available. ○ Only transport the patient when seizure resolves or it is otherwise safe to do so if seizure is not resolving.  **● Obtain** Blood Glucose Level (BGL)  **○ If** Blood Glucose Level is low (\<70mg/dl) **and** patient is able to swallow: **■ Administer** Oral Glucose Gel  **● Recheck** BGL after administration, repeat dose if necessary. |
| **AEMT+** |
| **● Establish** IV/IO access as indicated.  **● Administer** Dextrose 10% Solution IV/IO drip **if** hypoglycemia (BGL \<70mg/dl) is present **and** the patient is unable to swallow Oral Glucose Gel. |
| **Paramedic** |
| **● If** the patient is **actively seizing as a result of suspected eclampsia, or is hypertensive with an altered level of consciousness and/or visual disturbances: ○ Administer** Magnesium Sulfate 4g IV drip **or** 10g IM.  ■ **If** Magnesium Sulfate is ineffective:  **● Administer** Midazolam 10mg IM/IN **OR** 2-5mg IV/IO  ○ May repeat if necessary up to max total of 20mg.  **● Apply** Cardiac Monitor.  **● Obtain** 12-Lead ECG |
| **Critical Care Paramedic** |
| ● **If** the patient is in a gestational hypertensive state (SBP \>160 with or without neurological symptoms):  ○ **Administer** Labetalol 20mg, slow IV/IO push  ■ **If** the patient remains hypertensive, repeat 40mg at 10 minutes. |
